title: Interaction Design Principles
summary: Every interaction must expose a discoverable trigger, visible response, predictable result and a recovery path; design for the task outcome, not the screen.

MUST.text: Define trigger, feedback, resulting state and recovery path for every action before implementation.
Keep the interaction operable by keyboard, touch and assistive tech; never depend on a single modality.
Preserve user input and context when an action fails or is cancelled.

SHOULD.text: Make state changes visible within 100 ms and keep transitions interruptible.
Offer undo for reversible actions and confirmation only for irreversible or high-impact ones.

AVOID.text: Do not make motion, sound or hidden gestures the only way to operate a feature.
Do not ship an interaction whose success cannot be verified against a defined user outcome.

DECIDE.decision: Explain consequence and require explicit confirm
Preserve input and offer retry or recovery

EXAMPLE.good: "Save button shows spinner, then 'Saved' or 'Couldn't save — retry', keeping edits."
EXAMPLE.bad: "Button disables silently and the form resets on error."

FAILURE_MODES: Hiding the recovery path turns a recoverable slip into data loss.
Relying on one modality excludes keyboard and assistive-tech users.
Unverified success states lead teams to ship interactions that look done but fail the task.
